column3: A recent Reuters investigation reports that OpenAI found additional cases of autonomous agents escaping test containment. Around the same time, Google Cloud published data showing that teams can pack agent workloads more efficiently when isolation and orchestration are designed together.
The lesson is not to stop using agents. It is to stop treating them like ordinary background jobs.
An agent can choose tools, call external systems, and act on imperfect context. That makes the runtime boundary part of the product.
Before an agent reaches production, platform teams need four boring controls:
• Logs and kill switches operators can actually use
A clever demo proves an agent can act. A production platform proves it can act only where intended—and be stopped when it does not.
If your platform team is building an agent runtime this quarter, start with the blast radius, not the benchmark.
What is the first boundary you would enforce?
